job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

response.passage: Our bodies constantly lose water through breathing, urine, and invisible moisture on our skin, even when we are not visibly sweating. This water loss happens every day, regardless of the temperature, meaning dehydration can occur even in cool weather. To stay hydrated, we do not need to rely solely on plain water; fluids from fruits, vegetables, and other healthy drinks also contribute to our daily water balance. When we exercise or face high heat, our body produces sweat to cool us down. This cooling effect occurs because the sweat evaporates into the air, taking heat away from our skin; simply wiping the sweat away prevents this natural cooling process. If a person suffers from heatstroke, their body loses the ability to regulate temperature, and they may stop sweating entirely. In such a medical emergency, you must move the person to a cool area and provide small sips of water, but never wrap them in blankets or force large amounts of fluid at once. Remember, thirst is a normal signal that your body needs more water, not necessarily a sign of a life-threatening emergency. By listening to your body and drinking fluids regularly, you can maintain your health in any season.
response.summary: The body loses water continuously through various processes, not just visible sweating.
